title: Range of the averaged Gaussian indicator
statement: Let $n\ge0$, let $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be measurable, and let $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $x\in\mathbb R^n$. For $u_\theta(x)=\int 1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$, where $\gamma_n$ is standard Gaussian measure, one has $0\le u_\theta(x)\le1$.
replaced: Let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$. For $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ and $\theta\in\mathbb R$, put $u_\theta(x)=\int1_A(\cos\theta\,x+\sin\theta\,y)\,d\gamma_n(y)$. If $A$ is measurable, then $0\le u_\theta(x)\le1$ for every real $\theta$ and every $x$.
